propositions.text: The claimant seeks refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX seeks refugee protection pursuant to section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1

paragraphs.summary: The claimant seeks refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of IRPA.

propositions.text: The claimant appeared without counsel after his former counsel withdrew on July 6, 2010.
propositions.quote: The claimant's former counsel of record withdrew his services on July 6, 2010.

propositions.text: The claimant requested a 30-day adjournment to retain new counsel.
propositions.quote: The claimant sought an adjournment of 30 days in order to retain and instruct new counsel.

propositions.text: The panel inquired about the claimant's efforts to obtain counsel since July 6, 2010.
propositions.quote: The panel inquired as to what efforts the claimant had undertaken to obtain and instruct counsel since July 6, 2010.

propositions.text: The claimant spoke to two lawyers but neither agreed to represent him.
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he had spoken to two lawyers, but could not remember their full names, neither of whom agreed to represent him.

propositions.text: The panel considered factors in Rule 48(4) when deciding on the adjournment request.
propositions.quote: In considering the request for the adjournment, the panel took into account all the factors set out in Rule 48(4).2

propositions.text: The claimant had over two years to prepare and over two months to find new counsel before the hearing.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that the claimant had more than two years to prepare for the hearing. The claimant had more than two months to obtain and instruct new counsel in advance of the present hearing.

propositions.text: The claimant did not demonstrate serious effort to be ready to start the hearing by only approaching two lawyers.
propositions.quote: The claimant, in approaching only two other lawyers, did not demonstrate serious effort to be ready to start the hearing.

propositions.text: The panel denied the adjournment request as it would unreasonably delay proceedings.
propositions.quote: The panel determined that allowing the application would unreasonably delay the proceedings in all the circumstances of the present case. The panel therefore denied the request for a postponement.

propositions.text: The claimant indicated he would proceed without counsel if the adjournment was denied.
propositions.quote: The claimant indicated that he would proceed without counsel if the request for postponement were not granted.

propositions.text: After denying the adjournment, the panel confirmed the claimant was ready to proceed and he agreed.
propositions.quote: After denying the request, the panel confirmed with the claimant that he was ready to proceed and the claimant replied in the affirmative.

paragraphs.summary: The panel denied the claimant's 30-day adjournment request due to insufficient effort to find counsel and potential delay; claimant proceeded unrepresented.

propositions.text: The claimant was granted asylum in the USA in 2000 based on alleged Rwandan nationality and became a permanent resident in 2005.
propositions.quote: The claimant was granted asylum in the USA in XXXXX 2000 on the basis of his alleged Rwandan nationality. He obtained permanent resident status in the USA on that same basis in 2005.

propositions.text: In 2008, US DHS served notice to cancel asylum status due to belief claimant was Ugandan national.
propositions.quote: In 2008, the US Department of Homeland Security served notice on the claimant to cancel his asylum status, because they had information that led them to believe he was in fact a national of the Republic of Uganda.

propositions.text: The claimant requested a 90-day delay to gather evidence after receiving notice to appear for proceedings.
propositions.quote: The claimant received the notice to appear for this proceeding and requested a delay of 90 days for the purpose of gathering evidence.

propositions.text: After no response from US authorities, claimant visited Canada and learned asylum was cancelled and deportation hearing scheduled.
propositions.quote: Subsequent to his arrival, he learned that his asylum status had been cancelled when he failed to appear as convoked. He also received a copy of a notice to appear for a deportation hearing in the USA.

propositions.text: The claimant sought refugee protection in Canada after learning of US asylum cancellation and deportation hearing.
propositions.quote: He thereupon sought refugee protection in Canada.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges prior Rwandan nationality declarations were misrepresentations.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that his previous declarations of Rwandan nationality were misrepresentations.

propositions.text: In 1999, claimant was detained twice by Ugandan security due to acquaintance with suspected government opponent.
propositions.quote: The claimant now alleges that, in 1999, he was detained on two occasions by the security services of Uganda, because of his acquaintance with a XXXX in the Ugandan armed forces suspected of being an opponent of the government.

propositions.text: Claimant obtained US non-immigrant visa in 1999, entered USA, and applied for asylum in 2000.
propositions.quote: He subsequently obtained a US non-immigrant visa and entered the USA in XXXXXX 1999, and applied for asylum in the USA in XXXX, 2000.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant was granted US asylum as Rwandan, later faced cancellation due to alleged Ugandan nationality, then sought Canadian refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Minister served notice of intention to intervene via documents related to claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The Minister of Public Safety served notice of his intention to intervene in the present hearing by way of documents.3 The Minister's intervention related to the assessment of the credibility of the claimant, in light of information received from the US Department of Homeland Security.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister intervened to address the claimant's credibility based on US DHS information.

propositions.text: Exclusion was included as an issue in the hearing screening form dated April 22, 2010.
propositions.quote: it was included as an issue to be raised at the hearing in the screening form dated April 22, 2010.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied the claimant had adequate notice that exclusion would be raised.
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied that the claimant had adequate notice that this issue would be raised in the present hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the claimant had adequate notice that exclusion would be an issue at the hearing.

propositions.text: The panel determines on balance of probabilities that claimant has US permanent resident status and is excluded from refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The panel determines, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant has permanent resident status in the USA and is therefore excluded from Refugee Protection.

propositions.text: Alternatively, the panel finds claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of Canada's protection.
propositions.quote: In the alternative, the panel determines that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of Canada's protection.

propositions.text: The determinative issues were the claimant's identity and credibility.
propositions.quote: In arriving at the decision on inclusion, the determinative issues were the identity and credibility of the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant excluded due to US permanent resident status or alternatively not a refugee; identity and credibility were key issues.

propositions.text: The Schedule to IRPA provides relevant provisions.
propositions.quote: The Schedule to the IRPA provides in part as follows:

paragraphs.summary: The Schedule to IRPA provides relevant provisions.

propositions.text: Article 1E of the UN Refugee Convention excludes persons recognized as having nationality rights in their country of residence.
propositions.quote: SECTIONS E AND F OF ARTICLE 1 OF THE UNITED NATIONS CONVENTION RELATING TO THE STATUS OF REFUGEES: E. This Convention shall not apply to a person who is recognized by the competent authorities of the country in which he has taken residence as having the rights and obligations which are attached to the possession of the nationality of that country.4

paragraphs.summary: Article 1E of the UN Refugee Convention excludes persons recognized as nationals by their country of residence.

propositions.text: Documents seized included US Refugee Travel Document and permanent resident card valid 2005-2016.
propositions.quote: Among the documents seized by the Immigration Officer5 were a US Refugee Travel Document, identifying the bearer as enjoying permanent resident status in the USA, and a US permanent resident card. The card was issued XXXXXX, 2005 and valid to XXXXXX, 2016.

propositions.text: The claimant testified these documents were genuine and presented them at Pearson Airport in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that they were both genuine documents and that he had presented them both when he was granted admission as a temporary resident at Pearson Airport on XXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: Documents show claimant's US permanent resident status; claimant testified to their genuineness and use at Canadian entry.

propositions.text: Valid US permanent resident status triggers Article 1E exclusion under the Convention.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that valid and subsisting permanent resident status in the USA engages section 1E of the Convention.

propositions.text: Possession of a permanent resident card creates rebuttable presumption of status.
propositions.quote: The possession of a permanent resident card creates a rebuttable presumption that the claimant enjoys that status.

propositions.text: Claimant's asylum was terminated in 2008 but permanent resident status was not addressed then.
propositions.quote: It is clear from the documentation before the panel that the claimant's grant of asylum was terminated, effective XXXX, 2008.6 This notice did not however address the permanent resident status which followed the initial grant of asylum, some five years later.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he felt he lost permanent resident status in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he felt he no longer had permanent resident status as of XXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: The panel disagrees and finds claimant retains permanent resident status until deportation order issued.
propositions.quote: With respect, the panel does not agree. The claimant himself introduced a notice to appear for a deportation hearing scheduled for XXXX, 2008.7 The panel is satisfied that the claimant enjoys permanent resident status in the USA until the competent authority issues a deportation order against him.

propositions.text: Claimant chose not to appear at deportation hearing fearing removal from USA.
propositions.quote: The claimant declared that he chose not to appear for the deportation hearing because he feared subsequent removal from the USA.

propositions.text: US DHS disclosure states claimant failed to appear for termination interview; asylum terminated; no info on further action.
propositions.quote: In the Minister's disclosure dated June 23, 2010, the US Department of Homeland Security states in part: The individual failed to appear for his termination interview; thereafter his asylum status was terminated. The Asylum Office issued a Notice to Appear (NTA), but there was no information to indicate if any further action was taken.8

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant retains US permanent resident status despite asylum termination, supported by DHS disclosure and claimant's failure to appear at deportation hearing.

propositions.text: Minister's disclosure confirms claimant was subject to deportation hearing.
propositions.quote: The Minister's disclosure confirms the claimant's own evidence that he was the subject of a separate deportation hearing.

propositions.text: Panel finds no record of deportation order issued against claimant.
propositions.quote: The panel finds it reasonable to believe that if a deportation order had been made against the claimant at the June 16 hearing, or subsequently, the US authorities would have a record of that deportation and have disclosed it.

propositions.text: Claimant has no evidence of deportation order issued against him.
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant if he had any evidence that a deportation order had been issued to him and he replied that he had no such evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no evidence of a deportation order against claimant, supported by Minister's disclosure and claimant's testimony.

propositions.text: Panel is satisfied claimant is still a US permanent resident on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: After considering the whole of the documentary evidence before the panel and the claimant's testimony, the panel is satisfied that he is today still a permanent resident of the USA, on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimant is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E and s. 98 of IRPA.
propositions.quote: He is therefore subject to Article 1E of the Convention and excluded from refugee protection pursuant to s. 98 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant remains a US permanent resident and is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E and IRPA s. 98.

propositions.text: At hearing, claimant declined to affirm contents of Personal Information Form (PIF) but admitted signature.
propositions.quote: At the outset of the hearing, when the claimant was asked to affirm the contents of his Personal Information Form (PIF),9 the claimant declined to do so and testified that the PIF misrepresented the facts. The panel asked the claimant if he had signed the PIF at page 13, and he testified that it was his signature.

propositions.text: Claimant understood signature on PIF was equivalent to giving evidence under oath.
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant if he understood that the signature was equivalent to giving evidence under oath, and he replied that he understood this.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant declined to affirm the PIF contents but admitted signing it and understood it was evidence under oath.

propositions.text: The PIF contained multiple untruthful items including birthplace, nationality, family, education, arrest, residence, passport, and narrative.
propositions.quote: The panel proceeded to review the items in the PIF which were untruthful. They included the following items: * the claimant's place of birth; * the claimant's nationality, ethnicity and mother tongue; * the details of the claimant's marital status and family members; * the details of his alleged education and employment in Rwanda; * the alleged arrest by the government of Rwanda; * the details of his alleged residence in Rwanda; * the allegation that his Ugandan passport was improperly obtained; * the whole of his narrative.

propositions.text: Claimant said he assumed Rwandan identity to improve asylum chances in USA due to physical resemblance.
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he physically resembles a Rwandan ethnic Tutsi, and that he felt by assuming this nationality he would stand a greater chance of receiving asylum in the USA.

propositions.text: Claimant maintained false identity through US permanent residence and refugee travel document applications and living in USA for three years.
propositions.quote: He elected to continue maintaining that false identity through his application for permanent residence in the USA, his application for a US refugee travel document, and three years of living in that country as a permanent residence.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he resolved to be truthful in Canada but maintained false identity in Canadian applications until Minister's disclosure in 2010.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he resolved to be truthful in Canada. However, the panel notes that in both his application for protection made to the immigration officer10 and his PIF,11 he maintained his false identity. His change of heart appears to have come about only subsequent to the disclosure of the Minister of June 23, 2010.12

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant's PIF contained many falsehoods; claimant admitted assuming Rwandan identity to improve asylum chances and only changed after Minister's disclosure.

propositions.text: Claimant had no evidence to corroborate Ugandan identity or alleged persecution.
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant if he had any evidence to corroborate his alleged identity as a citizen of Uganda, and the alleged persecution he suffered in that country and he replied that he did not.

propositions.text: Only evidence on core issues is claimant's uncorroborated testimony.
propositions.quote: The only evidence on these core issues is the claimant's uncorroborated testimony.

propositions.text: Claimant's history of misrepresentation over eleven years reduces weight given to his testimony.
propositions.quote: However, the claimant has demonstrated a significant willingness to misrepresent his identity to officials in both Canada and the USA over a period of eleven years. In the circumstances, the panel gives little weight to the claimant's testimony about his identity and the alleged events in Uganda.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant's uncorroborated testimony on identity and persecution unreliable due to long history of misrepresentation.

propositions.text: Yip decision requires claimant to establish identity on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: In the Yip decision, the Federal Court held that the claimant has the fundamental obligation to establish his or her identity on a balance of probabilities.13

propositions.text: Kante decision affirms claimant must bring all evidence believed necessary to prove claim.
propositions.quote: In the Kante decision, the Court affirmed that the claimant must come to a hearing with all of the evidence that he or she is able to offer and believes is necessary to prove the claim.14

propositions.text: Rule 7 requires claimant to document identity and other claim elements.
propositions.quote: Rule 715 requires the claimant to document his identity and other elements of his claim.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to discharge burden to prove new Ugandan identity and nationality.
propositions.quote: With respect to his newly declared identity and Ugandan nationality the panel finds the claimant has not discharged this burden.

propositions.text: The panel does not know the claimant's true identity.
propositions.quote: The panel does not know who the claimant truly is.

paragraphs.summary: The panel applied precedent and rules to find claimant failed to prove his Ugandan identity and true identity remains unknown.

propositions.text: Section 106 IRPA requires considering documentation and explanations regarding claimant's identity for credibility.
propositions.quote: S. 106 of IRPA requires the panel to take into the account, with respect to the credibility of a claimant, whether the claimant possesses acceptable documentation establishing identity, and, if not, whether they have provided a reasonable explanation for the lack of documentation or have taken reasonable steps to obtain the documentation.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to satisfy statutory obligation on identity documentation, leading to negative credibility inference.
propositions.quote: In light of the analysis above, the panel finds that the claimant has not satisfied this statutory obligation and draws a negative inference on his credibility as a result.

propositions.text: Without knowing true identity, panel cannot find claimant faces serious persecution risk; not a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: Without knowing his true identity, the panel cannot be satisfied that the claimant faces a serious possibility of persecution on Convention grounds. He is not a Convention refugee, accordingly.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant failed to document identity, negatively affecting credibility and concluding he is not a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: Insufficient reliable evidence shows claimant faces danger of torture or risk to life or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: There is not sufficient, reliable evidence before the panel to suggest that the claimant faces a danger of torture or that, on a balance of probabilities, he faces a risk to his life or to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: He is not a person in need of protection, accordingly.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found no sufficient evidence claimant faces torture or risk and is not in need of protection.

propositions.text: The panel excludes claimant from refugee protection under s. 98 IRPA and alternatively rejects claim as not a refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the claimant is excluded from refugee protection pursuant to s. 98 of the IRPA. In the alternative, the panel determines that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee, nor a person in need of protection and therefore rejects his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel excludes claimant from refugee protection and alternatively rejects his claim as not a refugee or person in need of protection.
